questions.question: Is (Z, −) [integers under subtraction] a group?
questions.solutionApproach: Closure: yes (a−b is an integer). Associative: (a−b)−c ≠ a−(b−c) in general → FAILS. So not even a semigroup.
questions.answer: No — fails associativity, so it's not even a semigroup.

questions.question: Is (Z_6, +_6) [integers mod 6 under addition mod 6] a group? Is it abelian?
questions.solutionApproach: Closure: yes. Associative: yes (inherited from integer addition). Identity: 0. Inverse: every element a has inverse (6−a) mod 6. Commutative: yes. All hold → Abelian Group.

questions.question: G is a group with |G|=45. What is the size of the largest possible PROPER subgroup of G?
questions.solutionApproach: Divisors of 45 = {1,3,5,9,15,45}. Largest strictly less than 45 = 15.

questions.question: Prove: if a*a=e for every element a in group G, then G is abelian.
questions.solutionApproach: For any a,b∈G: (a*b)*(a*b)=e (given). Left-multiply by a, right-multiply by b: a*(a*b*a*b)*b = a*e*b ⟹ (a*a)*b*a*(b*b) = a*b ⟹ e*b*a*e = a*b ⟹ b*a = a*b. QED.
questions.answer: Proved — uses a*a=e (so a=a⁻¹ for every element) plus associativity.
